A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same INTUITOR/RLIF research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training experiments, benchmark evaluations, reward-exploitation tests, statistical analyses, and model-output case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds model evaluations and entropy/random-reward control results in Appendix A.

M1.justification: INTUITOR retains self-certainty rewards, group-normalized advantages, GRPO optimization, and online reward scoring. Additional model configurations and comparison rewards do not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain the existing mathematical and code corpora and the GSM8K, MATH500, LiveCodeBench, CRUXEval-O, MMLU-Pro, and AlpacaEval tasks. Added model evaluations and reward controls reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix A.4 adds entropy-minimization and random-reward GRPO controls, substantially broadening comparisons of reward choice. Figure 10 also adds GRPO to the previously INTUITOR-only Llama training comparison. Existing GRPO and GRPO-PV comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen3-14B and OLMo-2-1124-7B-SFT configurations and reward-control experiments using Qwen2.5-1.5B/3B. Existing splits, evaluation metrics, decoding instructions, and tabulated hyperparameters remain unchanged. The revised Table 4 scores do not establish an undisclosed protocol change.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.4 and Figure 12 directly investigate whether alternative intrinsic rewards or uninformative random rewards reproduce INTUITOR's benefits, reporting degeneration under both controls. These substantially extend reward-specificity analyses beyond the retained KL sweep, online/offline comparison, confidence analysis, and Appendix B case studies.

E5.justification: Figure 8 retains the same Mann–Whitney U tests, p-values, and effect sizes. The added experiments introduce no repeated-run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or new statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 4 revises numerous Qwen2.5 scores: the 7B GRPO/INTUITOR MATH500 comparison changes from 0.699/0.730 to 0.750/0.750. Qwen3 rows, Llama and OLMo benchmark tables, comparative training curves, and reward-control degeneration results are added. Tables 1–3 retain their results.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds an explicit mathematical definition of the entropy-control reward. Its printed -sum p log p expression has the positive-entropy sign despite the negative-entropy description. The self-certainty definition and existing formal framework remain; no new theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims of label-free self-certainty training, GRPO-comparable mathematical performance, improved transfer, and structured reasoning. The introduction's added Llama/OLMo sentence supplies supporting evidence without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.4 adds a repetition-trap explanation for entropy rewards without sufficient supervised training and interprets random-reward deterioration as evidence that INTUITOR's gains are nontrivial. Appendix A.1 removes the explanation attributing initial discrepancies to multi-node nondeterminism. Main-text limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4 specifies equiprobable binary random rewards and an entropy-scoring expression; A.1 removes the multi-node nondeterminism disclosure. The hyperparameter table, relocated from Table 5 to Table 7, retains its values. Training prompts, A100 hardware disclosure, and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds OLMo, Prabhudesai et al.'s confidence-maximization work, and Holtzman et al.'s neural-text-degeneration work. Appendix A.4 expands the contrast with entropy-based optimization. The established RLHF/RLVR/RLIF positioning is retained; the Llama reference is relocated, not newly added.

P1.justification: Changes include localized introduction edits, renaming A.1, adding Appendix A subsections, and renumbering the hyperparameter subsection. Most main-text prose and all Appendix B prompts and examples retain their wording.

P2.justification: Appendix displays expand substantially through new Tables 5–6, Figures 11–12, and a Qwen3 block in Table 4. Figure 10 changes from one dual-axis INTUITOR plot to two panels comparing GRPO and INTUITOR. The hyperparameter table moves, while the principal main-text displays remain largely intact.

improvement.justification: Explicit Llama/OLMo benchmark comparisons and the random-reward control improve empirical scrutiny beyond v1's limited Llama reporting and absent random control. The benefit is constrained by unexplained Table 4 score revisions and the entropy-control formula's sign conflict with its stated objective, which weakens that comparison. Overall, the revision provides modestly more informative evidence.
